clue.text: Feature of one lying with energy about opportunity that's returned at last

definitions.note: a greeting phrase said to someone who has finally come back after a long absence

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the next one, enclosing it

parts.note: a liar's tell-tale feature, as with Pinocchio, is a long nose
an opportunity is a time to do something, as in 'now is the time'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A description of a liar's tell, energised by some chance that has finally come back round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the opportunity sit inside the liar's feature. The definition describes the greeting by the person it is said to, who has finally come back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock greeting offered to a friend who has come back after a long absence.

clue.text: Didn't contribute as needed, with lots to play

definitions.text: Didn't contribute as needed, with lots to play
definitions.note: a sporting picture of a team member failing teammates while the game still has plenty left to run

indicators.note: to play suggests letters being toyed with and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team member failed to pull their weight while the match still had plenty left in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' rearranges NEEDED WITH LOTS. The whole clue also defines the answer: a sporting slacker failing teammates with lots of the game left.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to disappoint one's team or colleagues by failing to do one's part.

clue.text: Black piece, not king

indicators.note: not means the king's letter is left out of the piece

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess note: a dark piece that is not the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes K from KNIGHT. 'Black' looks like the colour of the chess piece but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark part of the day, so black as night is a synonym in crossword use.

clue.text: Over a tedious speech, announce a dance

indicators.note: over means the announcing word goes over, covering, the next pieces so they sit inside it

parts.note: to tell is to announce or make known
taken as written
a rant is a long, tiresome tirade
taken as written

explanation.surface: After sitting through a boring harangue, someone declares it time to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads like 'after' or 'finished' but is a container signal: the announcing word goes over the boring speech, which ends up inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast Neapolitan folk dance in six-eight time.

clue.text: Scholar overlooks sacred book: it is free

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that overlooks another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree
Num is the abbreviation for Numbers, a book of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholar studies a holy text and announces it is freely available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooks' works only in a down light: the scholar sits above the sacred book. 'is' links to the definition, and 'free' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To manumit is to release a slave from bondage, which is to set them free.

clue.text: Greeting by title, when introducing a second time

indicators.note: introducing means the following pieces are put into the title

parts.note: a name is a title someone goes by
taken as written

explanation.surface: A greeting given by title when someone is being introduced again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' puts A, S and T inside NAME, between its M and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Namaste is the Hindu salutation spoken with palms pressed together, a greeting.

clue.text: Active resistance agent is about

indicators.note: about means the agent wraps around the resistance letter

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An active member of the Resistance reports that an enemy agent is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside SPY; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone lively and nimble, especially for their age, so active.

clue.text: Extension of deadline that may avoid penalties

definitions.meaning: more time granted beyond an agreed cut-off
in football, the added period played before a match goes to a penalty shoot-out

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means additional time allowed, and in knockout football the added half hour before penalties.

clue.text: Understand stingy type is to act boldly

parts.note: to grasp something is to understand it
a stinging plant, the nettle, read as 'stingy' in the sense of stinging rather than mean

explanation.surface: Get to know the miser, which takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stingy' suggests meanness but here means having a sting, so the type is the nettle; 'is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to tackle a difficulty head on, boldly, as a firmly gripped nettle does not sting.

clue.text: Soldier held back in short period — he got his stripes

indicators.note: held means the reversed soldier is contained in the shortened period
short means the period loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is a period of time

indicators.note: back means the soldier's letters are turned round

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier detained in a brief spell finally earned promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the soldier round, 'short' trims the period and 'held' puts one inside the other. 'got his stripes' sounds like a promotion to sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is the animal with a striped coat, cryptically described as having earned stripes.

clue.text: Figure fractionally superior

definitions.meaning: the number written on top in a fraction

explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction the upper number is called this, and it is itself a figure.

clue.text: Hello: girl's put on brown dress at first with no pattern

indicators.note: put on means the girl follows, placed onto the preceding pieces

parts.note: hi is an informal hello
tan is a light brown

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of dress is used

parts.note: miss is a young girl; 's here stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A greeting, then a girl is wearing a brown dress with no pattern on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like getting dressed but places the girl after the colour and the dress's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done randomly, succeeding only sometimes, follows no pattern.

clue.text: Lots of boasts right out

indicators.note: out means the right letter is removed from the boasts

parts.note: brags means boasts

explanation.surface: Plenty of bragging is just out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R from BRAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, bags of something means plenty of it, lots of.

clue.text: Write prejudiced description of war

parts.note: to pen is to write
insular means narrow-minded and prejudiced

explanation.surface: Writing a biased account of a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peninsular War was fought in Spain and Portugal against Napoleon; the adjective names it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the adjective that names the Napoleonic campaign in Iberia, the Peninsular War.

clue.text: Believing group will keep us quiet? Doubtful

indicators.note: will keep means the group holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a sect is a group sharing a belief
taken as written
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: Will a religious group keep us silent? It seems unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will keep' puts the two small pieces inside the group; the question mark dresses the surface and the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspect as an adjective means open to doubt, questionable.

clue.text: Czar's aunt relocated in South American city

indicators.note: relocated means these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the word Czar's provides its letters including the S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler's aunt has moved to live in a Latin American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocated' rearranges CZARS plus AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Cruz is a large city in Bolivia, in South America.

clue.text: Point to one knowing the law, a reflective writer

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
a legist is an expert in law

explanation.surface: Directed towards a legal expert, a thoughtful author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, mournful and meditative poems, so is a reflective writer.

clue.text: Glad end — criminal was on gibbet?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A happy ending for a criminal who swung from the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal for GLAD END.
explanation.definitionFit: A body on a gibbet hung swinging loosely, which is what the verb describes.

clue.text: Swallow in air moving

definitions.meaning: a current of air in a room

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a single swig of liquid and a cold current of air.

clue.text: African sugar inspires passion

indicators.note: inspires is read as breathes in, so the sugar takes the passion inside

parts.note: cane is sugar cane, a source of sugar
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: An African sugar crop stirs up strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' is read literally, as breathing in. The answer is a native of Cairo, so 'African' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cairene is a person from Cairo, the Egyptian capital, so an African.

clue.text: To commander, man is so important

definitions.text: To commander, man is so important

parts.words: To commander, man is so important
parts.note: the three letters m-a-n sit in the very middle of the word commander, so to that word they are at the heart

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'so important' as the definition, then note that MAN stands exactly at the middle of comMANder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something central is of key importance, and it also means located in the middle.

clue.text: Attraction of daughter, naked

parts.note: raw can mean bare or naked

explanation.surface: The appeal of an unclothed daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is something that pulls in crowds, an attraction.

clue.text: The sort of fussy rule that gets your goat?

definitions.text: The sort of fussy rule that gets your goat?

parts.words: The sort of fussy rule that gets your goat?
parts.note: an overprotective government which irritates people, with a nod to the female goat

explanation.definitionFit: The term describes an interfering government that treats citizens like children needing a nursemaid.

clue.text: Judge avoiding obscure language That's elementary

indicators.note: avoiding means the judge's letter is dropped from the language

parts.note: jargon is specialist, obscure language

explanation.surface: A judge steers clear of legal mumbo-jumbo: that's basic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes J from JARGON. 'That's elementary' sounds like Holmes but means a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a chemical element, a noble gas, so it is elementary in that sense.

clue.text: Ground that's high or low, by river

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Land that is upland or lowland beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like the opposite of high but is a verb: what a cow does. 'or' and 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A moor is an open tract of upland ground, so high ground.

clue.text: Aggressor passionate for extended period, losing head

parts.note: warm can mean ardent or passionate

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: longer means for a more extended period

explanation.surface: A fiery aggressor who loses his cool over a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes L from LONGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A warmonger stirs up war, so is an aggressor.

clue.text: Such theatre backed by 9 changing hands

indicators.note: backed means the altered word is read in reverse
changing hands means its right letter is swapped for a left one

parts.note: refers to the answer at 9 across, the striped animal

explanation.surface: A kind of theatre supported by an investor at number nine who swaps hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' swaps R (right) for L (left) in TIGER, giving TIGEL; 'backed' turns that round. Legit theatre is the conventional stage as opposed to music hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate or legit theatre is serious drama, as distinct from variety and revue.

clue.text: Love to play, given strict rule enforcement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
play in a mechanism, the slack allowed, is a tolerance

explanation.surface: A passion for games, combined with a stickler's approach to the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' means slack in a mechanism, not games. 'to' and 'given' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a policy of punishing every infringement, however minor, so strict enforcement.
